errors.io: Could not read or write a file.
errors.pack: Packing failed — see the build log for details.
errors.blocked: Your antivirus blocked runtime files in the .carafe service folder inside the library — the build log lists them. These are Wine DLLs from the Autorun repository: Carafe verified their checksums before the build, and antivirus heuristics sometimes mistake them for a threat. Add the .carafe folder to the exclusions (Windows Security → Virus & threat protection → Manage settings → Exclusions) and build again.
errors.noSpace: There is not enough space for the build on the drive with the library folder — the build log shows how much is needed and how much is free. While a game is being built, it takes up about four times the size of the finished NSP together with the Carafe runtime. Free up space on the drive or choose a library folder on another drive in Settings.
errors.pathTooLong: The path to one of the game files in the build folder is longer than the hacBrewPack packer can read — the build log shows the longest path and the limit. Non-Latin letters count as two or three characters. Shorten the path: move the library folder closer to the root of the drive (in Settings) or give the game folder a shorter name — its name is part of the path too.
errors.runtimeDamaged: Carafe runtime files are missing, unreadable or changed — the build log lists them. Most often this is the antivirus: its heuristics sometimes mistake Wine DLLs from the Autorun repository for a threat and quarantine them. Restore the files from quarantine (Windows Security → Virus & threat protection → Protection history) or reinstall Carafe, add the Carafe folder to the exclusions and build again.
errors.device: The Switch is not responding. Check that DBI is open in MTP mode.
errors.network: The website is not responding. Check your internet connection and try again.
errors.apiKey: The SteamGridDB API key is missing or was rejected — check it in the settings.
errors.unsupported: This file is not an image Carafe can read.
errors.icon: Could not make the icon — see the build log for details.
errors.invalid: The data did not pass validation.
errors.busy: A build or a USB install is running — wait for it to finish.

onboarding.welcomeText: Carafe turns a Windows game into a Switch app.
onboarding.keysText: A Switch app is encrypted with your console’s keys. They live in a prod.keys file that you dump from the console once with Lockpick_RCM:
onboarding.keysStep1: Reboot into Hekate, open Payloads and launch Lockpick_RCM.
onboarding.keysStep2: Choose Dump from sysNAND — the keys are saved to switch/prod.keys on the microSD card.
onboarding.keysStep3: Move the file to your PC: in Hekate, Tools → USB Tools → SD Card, or take the card out.
onboarding.keysNoLockpick: CFW packs usually include Lockpick_RCM. If it isn’t under Payloads, put Lockpick_RCM.bin into bootloader/payloads on the microSD card.
onboarding.keysOk: Required keys found: header_key and key_area_key_application_00.
onboarding.keysPrivacy: Carafe reads the keys only while packing and never copies them.
onboarding.libraryText: Carafe puts finished NSPs here. Each file keeps its own settings, so the folder can move to another computer.
onboarding.noticeSource: Games run through Autorun, an open-source project that brings Wine to the Switch. Carafe uses its prebuilt files and checks them before every build.
onboarding.noticeDefender: Windows Defender sometimes flags individual Wine DLLs. If a file goes missing, Carafe stops the build and shows how to add an exclusion.
onboarding.noticeWarranty: Carafe is free, open-source software. It comes as is, with no warranty, and you use it at your own risk.

wizard.folderMissing: The game folder is no longer where it was — point to its new location.

warnings.installerSelected: This looks like an installer or uninstaller, not the game itself.
warnings.onlyInstallers: The folder only has installers. Install the game on this PC and pick its folder.

art.noImages: This game has no square covers.
art.keyNeeded: Searching SteamGridDB needs your personal API key — it is free and entered once.
art.keyRejected: SteamGridDB rejected the key. Check it or create a new one.

art.keyStep2: Profile → Preferences → API: create a key.
art.keyStep3: Paste the key here and press Save.

build.done: Done. The game is in your library.
build.doneRebuild: Done. Install it over the old one — your progress stays.

input.modeKeyboardHint: Switch buttons press keys and mouse buttons. Suits most older games.
input.modeControllerHint: The game sees an Xbox 360 controller. Suits games with gamepad support.
input.deadzoneHint: The part of stick travel that doesn’t count as a tilt: it hides Joy-Con drift. Stick feels sluggish — lower it to 0–2; character creeps on its own — raise it.
input.keyboardAutoHint: Appears when the game waits for text input.

controls.pressOrPick: Press a key or a combination — or pick a mouse action:

direct3dHints.dxvk: Translates Direct3D 8–11 to Vulkan. The fastest path; suits almost every game.
direct3dHints.dxvkVkd3d: DXVK plus VKD3D for DirectX 12 games. Only they need it, and only 64-bit ones.
direct3dHints.wine: Direct3D through OpenGL, as in regular Wine. Slower; pick it if the game won’t start with DXVK or draws garbage.

dxvkSourceHints.official: The DXVK build that ships with Carafe.
dxvkSourceHints.gplasync: Carafe doesn’t ship GPL Async: the game will most likely fall back to the slow WineD3D. Keep “Official”.
dxvkSourceHints.sarek: Carafe doesn’t ship Sarek: the game will most likely fall back to the slow WineD3D. Keep “Official”.

graphics.frameLimitHint: Keeps the game from drawing faster than this: smoother frames, less heat and battery drain. The Switch screen runs at 60 Hz. Applies to Vulkan, DXVK and VKD3D.
graphics.hudHint: Frame rate and DXVK details over the game, to judge speed. It also changes how DXVK draws, so keep it off for playing.

upscalingHints.off: Stretches the picture to the screen with a slight blur.
upscalingHints.fsr: AMD FSR 1.0: stretches more crisply and adds sharpening. Good for old low-resolution games.
upscalingHints.integer: Every pixel becomes an even square — for pixel art. Only pictures up to 640×360 get enlarged; otherwise you get black borders.

graphics.upscalingScope: Works when the game draws below 1280×720 through Vulkan, DXVK or VKD3D.
graphics.sharpnessHint: Lower it if small text gets a bright halo.
graphics.vsyncHint: Frames change together with the screen refresh — no tearing. Off can be faster but tears. Overrides the game’s own setting; applies to Vulkan, DXVK and VKD3D.
graphics.lsfgHint: Inserts a generated frame between game frames: smoother, with slightly delayed controls. Needs Lossless.dll from your own copy of Lossless Scaling — a Carafe NSP can’t carry it yet, so this setting does nothing for now.
graphics.lsfgPerformanceHint: Faster, with less accurate in-between frames.
graphics.lsfgFlowHint: Resolution used to find motion: lower is faster, higher is more accurate.

advanced.title: Advanced

syncHints.horizon: Game threads wait for each other directly through the Switch kernel. Faster and more reliable; helps games that hang on start or show a black screen.
syncHints.standard: As in regular Wine — through a service thread. Pick it if the game misbehaves with Horizon.

cpuHints.fex: The main x86 emulator, for 32- and 64-bit games.
cpuHints.box64: A second emulator, for 32-bit games only. Try it if the game crashes or stutters with FEX.

windowsHints.auto: The compositor assembles the game’s windows — Carafe’s loading screen and cursor rely on it.
windowsHints.framebuffer: Windows are copied straight to the screen, without the compositor. A fallback if windows show up wrong; Carafe’s loading screen and cursor may not work.

advanced.fourCoresHint: Rendering and shaders run on the fourth core while the game keeps the other three to itself. Usually best left on.
advanced.verboseHint: A detailed Wine log in a separate file. Slows the game down a lot — only for hunting bugs.
advanced.profileHint: Logs where the game spends time. Slows the start down.

settings.title: Settings
settings.keysIncomplete: This file lacks the required keys — builds will fail.
settings.steamGridDbHint: Needed to search for covers. Get it at steamgriddb.com → sign in → Preferences → API.
settings.defaultsHint: The wizard starts from these. Games already built stay as they are.
settings.resetConfirm: Restore the recommended settings for new games? Controls, button layout and graphics will become what Carafe recommends for the Switch. Games already built won’t change.

updatesHint.automatic: Twice a day Carafe looks at its releases page on GitHub and downloads a new version in the background. It installs only when you ask. The check sends nothing else.
updatesHint.notifyOnly: Twice a day Carafe looks at its releases page on GitHub and shows a button in the library. It downloads only when you ask.
updatesHint.off: Carafe doesn’t contact GitHub on its own. Check with the button below.

update.title: Carafe update
update.runtimeChanged: The runtime is updated: afterwards, rebuild your games to give them the fixes.
update.downloadingHint: Keep working as usual. When it’s downloaded, this button offers a restart.
update.readyHint: Your library, settings and built games stay as they are. The restart takes a few seconds.
update.onCloseSet: The update installs when you close Carafe.
update.busyHint: A build or a USB install is running — restarting now would interrupt it.

download.title: The update didn’t download
download.text: The download stopped. Nothing in Carafe has changed.

verify.title: The update failed the check
verify.text: The downloaded file isn’t signed for this release, so Carafe won’t install it. Nothing in Carafe has changed.

install.title: The update didn’t install
install.text: The installer didn’t finish, and Carafe is still on {{version}}. Your library and settings are untouched.

update.found: Carafe {{version}} is out — see the button in the library
update.devBuild: This development build doesn’t update itself.

rebuild.offerTitle_one: {{count}} game is built with an older runtime
rebuild.offerTitle_other: {{count}} games are built with an older runtime
rebuild.offerText: Rebuilding gives them the fixes of runtime {{version}}.
rebuild.title: Rebuild with runtime {{version}}
rebuild.intro: Games are built one by one with the same settings, Title ID and icon. The old NSP is replaced only after a successful build.
rebuild.nothing: Every game is built with the current runtime. Nothing to rebuild.
rebuild.space: Needs up to {{size}} of free space on the library drive
rebuild.reinstallHint: Install each rebuilt game on the Switch again. Your saves on the console stay: the Title ID is the same.
